Loads normally. likely_cause.reasoning: Inference. The registration was not lost or re-created: the registry record shows a creation date of 2010-12-07, an expiry of 2030-12-07, client delete/renew/transfer/update locks and registrar GoDaddy, with GoDaddy nameservers (ns23/ns24.domaincontrol.com), so this is not a lapsed-then-reregistered domain. An Internet Archive capture of the same URL from 2026-04-20 still shows the genuine roofing site (WordPress page, Monroe Township, state licence 13VH01287400, contact form), so the replacement happened between then and today. The domain still resolves to a single IP whose reverse name is in host.secureserver.net (GoDaddy hosting) behind an anycast network, which is consistent with the site's files being replaced inside a hosting account rather than the name being moved to a third-party host. That points to a compromised or unauthorised change to the site or hosting content; only the owner's registrar and hosting account logs can confirm how access was obtained. An abandoned or parked-with-monetisation explanation cannot be fully excluded from public data.

fix_steps.step: Confirm who holds the GoDaddy account for biondoroofing.com, that the domain is set to auto-renew, and that two-step verification is on. The domain is already paid to 7 Dec 2030, so the fix is about account access, not renewal.
fix_steps.who: Owner plus whoever originally set up the website or domain

fix_steps.step: In the hosting account that serves the domain, find and remove the gambling page, restore the site from the most recent clean backup, then change the hosting, WordPress (the archived site ran on WordPress) and email passwords. If no clean backup exists, keep the domain serving a holding page until a replacement is ready.
fix_steps.who: Web developer, with the owner on the account

fix_steps.step: Publish a simple one-page site at the domain straight away: company name, services, towns served, phone, licence number and a few job photos, with a contact form. A static page or page-builder template keeps it from being overwritten again.

Repair the places customers are sent: edit the website field on the Google Business Profile so it points to a working page, then update or remove the old link on the AECinfo, FindTrustedRoofers and biondo-contracting.webflow.io entries.
fix_steps.who: Owner or office manager; developer for the directory edits

fix_steps.step: Once the spam is gone, use Search Console's Removals tool to temporarily block the gambling URL from results and the Refresh Outdated Content tool to update stale results, then add uptime plus content-change monitoring so a repeat replacement is noticed within a day.

after_fix.opportunity: Add an online quote request (with roof-photo upload) and a tap-to-call button, linked from the Google profile, so enquiries stop depending on a phone call.
after_fix.evidence: The Google profile lists 4.9 with the address, hours and phone (732) 257-2926, and its website field points at the broken domain; Birdeye shows 4.7 from 172 reviews. No live page we opened offers a form or booking - the Webflow page has none and the domain shows a gambling page - while the archived April 2026 version of the site had a contact form, so the rebuilt page would restore that and add photo upload.

# Website Health Check: Biondo Contracting

## What we saw on 13 November 2026

- biondoroofing.com, the site on your Google profile, loads over HTTPS but shows a Thai slot-gambling page styled as a Google Play listing ("4.9 star", 419K reviews); no roofing content is visible (screenshots kept).
- Your Google profile "Biondo Contracting-Roofing Specialists" (4.9, 38 Spotswood Ave, Monroe Township, (732) 257-2926) still links to it.
- The domain has not lapsed: registry data shows 2010 registration, paid to 7 December 2030, GoDaddy locks, and an archive copy from 20 April 2026 still shows your roofing site.
- AECinfo and FindTrustedRoofers still publish the domain, and a Webflow page headed "Biondoroofing.com" links to it.

## What it means for customers

A homeowner who taps the website on your profile lands on a gambling page and finds no services, towns served or quote form. The phone number is still listed on your profile, AECinfo and Birdeye, so enquiries depend on a call.

## How to fix it

1. Confirm who holds the GoDaddy account and turn on two-step verification (owner and site builder, 0.5-1 hour).
2. Remove the gambling page in the hosting account, restore the last clean backup, change site passwords (developer, 1-3 hours).
3. Publish a simple one-page site: services, towns, phone, licence number, photos, contact form (developer, 2-4 hours).
4. Update the website field on Google plus the AECinfo, FindTrustedRoofers and Webflow links (owner, 1-2 hours).
5. Block the gambling URL in Search Console's Removals tool, refresh stale results, add monitoring (developer, 1-2 hours).

## After the fix

Add an online quote request with photo upload and a tap-to-call button linked from the profile; your archived site had a contact form, which this restores.

Prepared from publicly available information on 13 November 2026. We did not log in to or change anything.
